newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to sell up to five firms before year-end.
newsitem.headline: Poland to sell up to five firms before year-end.

text.p: The Polish treasury ministry said on Monday it would sell between three and five companies before the end of the year.

Deputy treasury minister Wielaw Kaczmarek said the ministry planned to sell majority stakes in the Lezask SA brewery in the south-eastern town of Lezajsk, the bathroom furnishings producer CERSANIT SA from the eastern town of Karsnystaw and the electric engine maker Emit SA, based in the central town of Zychlin. @
"It think it will be realistic to close the privatisations of Emit from Zychlin, one of our last bathroom furnishings maker still state-owned Kranystaw, and Lezajsk," he told a news briefing.
He added the ministry would also try sell two meat-processing companies this year -- ZM Miestar SA, based in the southern city of Tarnow, and ZM Mazury SA, based in the northern city of Elk.
Kaczmarek also said that this year the ministry would approve issue prospectuses of four companies seeking Warsaw Stock Exchange listing next year. @
The companies are paper maker Swiecie SA, non-farrous metal producer Hutmen SA, white appliances maker Polar SA and metal trader Impexmetal SA.
Kaczmarek confirmed that apart from the KGHM copper combine, the ministry would also float the tourist agency Orbis SA.
Privatisations in the pharmaceutical, sugar and, possibly, the oil sector can also be expected, he added.
